statements.label: supported
statements.text: The number of multivesicular bodies increased during senescence in vivo.
statements.evidence: We find an increase in the number of multivesicular bodies during senescence in vivo.
statements.note: The study reports more multivesicular bodies during senescence in vivo.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Small extracellular vesicles transmit senescence more efficiently than soluble factors.
statements.evidence: both the soluble factors and small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) are capable of transmitting paracrine senescence to nearby cells
statements.note: The abstract states both can transmit paracrine senescence but never compares their relative efficiency.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Cells taking up small extracellular vesicles showed a positive correlation between sEV uptake and senescence activation.
statements.evidence: show a positive correlation between sEV uptake and senescence activation
statements.note: A Cre-reporter analysis found sEV uptake positively correlated with senescence activation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mass spectrometry and a functional siRNA screen identified IFITM3 as partially responsible for transmitting senescence to normal cells.
statements.evidence: interferon-induced transmembrane protein 3 (IFITM3) as being partially responsible for transmitting senescence to normal cells
statements.note: An MS and siRNA screen pinpointed IFITM3 as partly mediating senescence transmission.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Hematopoietic stem cell division rates are higher in mice and humans with atherosclerosis.
statements.evidence: hematopoietic stem cell division rates are increased in mice and humans with atherosclerosis
statements.note: The study found elevated HSC division rates in atherosclerotic mice and humans.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The elevated division rate in atherosclerosis patients is sufficient to produce a 3.5-fold increased risk of clonal hematopoiesis by age 70.
statements.evidence: sufficient to produce a 3.5-fold increased risk of clonal hematopoiesis by age 70
statements.note: Modeling the measured division-rate rise yields a 3.5-fold higher clonal hematopoiesis risk by age 70.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Reducing hematopoietic stem cell proliferation lowers cardiovascular mortality in patients.
statements.evidence: increased hematopoietic stem cell proliferation is an important factor contributing to the association between cardiovascular disease and clonal hematopoiesis
statements.note: The abstract names proliferation a contributing factor but never tests reducing it or any mortality outcome.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Expansion of competitively transplanted Tet2 -/- cells was accelerated under chronically elevated hematopoietic activity.
statements.evidence: expansion of competitively transplanted Tet2 -/- cells is accelerated under conditions of chronically elevated hematopoietic activity
statements.note: In mouse models, high hematopoietic activity sped the expansion of Tet2-null clones.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: ROS scavengers prevent senescence in PGAM5-deleted retinal pigment epithelial cells.
statements.evidence: cellular ATP and reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels are elevated
statements.note: The abstract reports elevated ROS after PGAM5 loss but tests no ROS-scavenging intervention.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Deletion of the mitochondrial phosphatase PGAM5 accelerated retinal pigment epithelial senescence in vitro and in vivo.
statements.evidence: deletion of mitochondrial phosphatase PGAM5 leads to accelerated retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) senescence in vitro and in vivo
statements.note: Removing PGAM5 sped RPE senescence in both cell and animal models.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: PGAM5 deletion increased mitochondrial fusion and decreased mitochondrial turnover.
statements.evidence: PGAM5 deletion leads to increased mitochondrial fusion and decreased mitochondrial turnover
statements.note: Loss of PGAM5 shifted mitochondria toward fusion and reduced their turnover.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Young but not aging Pgam5 -/- mice were resistant to sodium iodate-induced RPE cell death.
statements.evidence: Young but not aging Pgam5 -/- mice are resistant to sodium iodate-induced RPE cell death.
statements.note: Resistance to sodium iodate damage appeared only in young Pgam5-null mice.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with ABT263, PZ15227 is less toxic to platelets but equally or slightly more potent against senescent cells.
statements.evidence: Compared to ABT263, PZ is less toxic to platelets, but equally or slightly more potent against SCs because CRBN is poorly expressed in platelets
statements.note: PZ15227 spares platelets yet matches or exceeds ABT263's potency against senescent cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: PZ15227 cleared senescent cells and rejuvenated tissue stem and progenitor cells in naturally aged mice without causing severe thrombocytopenia.
statements.evidence: PZ effectively clears SCs and rejuvenates tissue stem and progenitor cells in naturally aged mice without causing severe thrombocytopenia
statements.note: In aged mice, PZ removed senescent cells and renewed stem/progenitor cells without severe platelet loss.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: PROTAC technology converted navitoclax (ABT263) into PZ15227, which targets Bcl-xl to the cereblon E3 ligase for degradation.
statements.evidence: converting it into PZ15227 (PZ), a Bcl-xl PROTAC, which targets Bcl-xl to the cereblon (CRBN) E3 ligase for degradation
statements.note: The authors reengineered ABT263 into a Bcl-xl PROTAC that routes Bcl-xl to CRBN for degradation.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: PZ15227 extended the lifespan of naturally aged mice.
statements.evidence: Small molecules that selectively kill senescent cells (SCs), termed senolytics, have the potential to prevent and treat various age-related diseases and extend healthspan
statements.note: Lifespan extension is mentioned only as a general senolytic prospect; no PZ lifespan result is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: As proliferating cells grow larger, concentration changes typical of cellular senescence become increasingly pronounced.
statements.evidence: As proliferating cells grow larger, concentration changes typically associated with cellular senescence are increasingly pronounced
statements.note: Bigger proliferating cells showed stronger senescence-associated proteome shifts.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Size-dependent proteome changes, including senescence-associated ones, were absent when cell size increased together with ploidy.
statements.evidence: Size-dependent changes to the proteome, including those associated with senescence, are not observed when an increase in cell size is accompanied by an increase in ploidy
statements.note: Raising ploidy alongside size prevented the senescence-linked proteome changes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Size-dependent protein concentration changes are driven more by mRNA levels than by protein turnover.
statements.evidence: Size-dependent protein concentration changes are widespread and predicted by subcellular localization, size-dependent mRNA concentrations, and protein turnover
statements.note: The abstract lists three predictors together but does not rank their relative contributions.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Larger cells were more prone to replicative, DNA-damage-induced, and CDK4/6i-induced senescence.
statements.evidence: larger cells are prone to replicative, DNA-damage-induced, and CDK4/6i-induced senescence
statements.note: Enlarged cells more readily entered several forms of senescence.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Caloric restriction reduced the incidence of chronic disease in the CALERIE participants.
statements.evidence: a conclusive test of the geroscience hypothesis will require trials with long-term follow-up to establish effects of intervention on primary healthy-aging endpoints, including incidence of chronic disease and mortality
statements.note: The abstract frames chronic-disease and mortality endpoints as future work and reports no such outcome.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the CALERIE trial, 220 adults without obesity were randomized to 25% caloric restriction or an ad libitum control diet for two years.
statements.evidence: n = 220 adults without obesity were randomized to 25% CR or ad libitum control diet for 2 yr
statements.note: The randomized trial assigned 220 non-obese adults to 25% CR or control for two years.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The caloric-restriction intervention slowed the pace of aging as measured by the DunedinPACE DNA methylation algorithm.
statements.evidence: CALERIE intervention slowed the pace of aging, as measured by the DunedinPACE DNAm algorithm
statements.note: DunedinPACE showed a slower aging pace under caloric restriction.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Caloric restriction did not significantly change biological age estimates from DNA methylation clocks including PhenoAge and GrimAge.
statements.evidence: did not lead to significant changes in biological age estimates measured by various DNAm clocks including PhenoAge and GrimAge
statements.note: PhenoAge and GrimAge clock estimates were unchanged by the intervention.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The biological age of young mice increased under heterochronic parabiosis and was restored after surgical detachment.
statements.evidence: the biological age of young mice is increased by heterochronic parabiosis and restored following surgical detachment
statements.note: Joining to old partners raised young mice's biological age, which reverted once separated.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Biological age rose rapidly in response to diverse stresses and reversed following recovery.
statements.evidence: biological age undergoes a rapid increase in response to diverse forms of stress, which is reversed following recovery from stress
statements.note: Stress drove a fast rise in biological age that recovery undid.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Transient changes in biological age occurred during major surgery, pregnancy, and severe COVID-19 in humans and/or mice.
statements.evidence: transient changes in biological age during major surgery, pregnancy, and severe COVID-19 in humans and/or mice
statements.note: The study detected temporary biological-age shifts across surgery, pregnancy, and severe COVID-19.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Pharmacologically reducing stress-induced biological age extends lifespan.
statements.evidence: The elevation of biological age by stress may be a quantifiable and actionable target for future interventions
statements.note: The abstract proposes stress-driven elevation as a future target but reports no lifespan intervention.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Whole-body B cell depletion restored proper lipolysis and core body temperature maintenance during cold stress.
statements.evidence: whole-body B cell depletion restores proper lipolysis and core body temperature maintenance during cold stress
statements.note: Removing B cells rescued lipolysis and cold-induced temperature control.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: A high-fat diet triggers the Nlrp3 inflammasome activation that drives aged adipose B cell expansion.
statements.evidence: the age-induced FALC formation, AAB, and splenic ABC expansion is dependent on the Nlrp3 inflammasome
statements.note: The abstract shows Nlrp3 dependence but never addresses what activates the inflammasome, such as diet.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Aged adipose B cells showed greater expansion in female mice.
statements.evidence: show greater expansion in female mice
statements.note: Expansion of these B cells was larger in females.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Inhibiting IL-1 signaling reduced aged adipose B cell proliferation and increased lipolysis in aging.
statements.evidence: inhibition of IL-1 signaling reduces their proliferation and increases lipolysis in aging
statements.note: Blocking IL-1 cut AAB proliferation and raised lipolysis in aged tissue.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Decreased IGF1 levels in the middle-aged bone marrow microenvironment are a factor causing hematopoietic stem cell aging.
statements.evidence: decreased levels of the longevity-associated molecule IGF1 in the local middle-aged BM microenvironment are a factor causing HSC aging
statements.note: Lower local IGF1 in the middle-aged marrow helps drive HSC aging.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Hallmarks of aging in HSCs and hematopoiesis begin to accumulate by middle age, with the bone marrow microenvironment indispensable for this aging.
statements.evidence: hallmarks of aging in HSCs and hematopoiesis begin to accumulate by middle age and that the bone marrow (BM) microenvironment at middle age induces and is indispensable for hematopoietic aging
statements.note: Aging hallmarks emerge by middle age and require the marrow microenvironment.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Direct stimulation of middle-aged HSCs with IGF1 rescued molecular and functional aging hallmarks, including restored mitochondrial activity.
statements.evidence: Direct stimulation of middle-aged HSCs with IGF1 rescues molecular and functional hallmarks of aging, including restored mitochondrial activity
statements.note: Giving IGF1 directly to middle-aged HSCs reversed aging hallmarks and restored mitochondria.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: IGF1 supplementation improves immune function in elderly humans.
statements.evidence: Decline in hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) function with age underlies limited health span of our blood and immune systems.
statements.note: The abstract links HSC decline to blood and immune health in mice but tests no IGF1 treatment in elderly humans.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Aging clocks revealed that heterochronic parabiosis and exercise both reverse transcriptomic aging in neurogenic regions, but in different ways.
statements.evidence: heterochronic parabiosis and exercise reverse transcriptomic aging in neurogenic regions, but in different ways
statements.note: Both interventions reversed transcriptomic aging, through distinct patterns.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The regression models predicted biological age more accurately than chronological age.
statements.evidence: We trained single-cell-based regression models to predict chronological age and biological age (neural stem cell proliferation capacity)
statements.note: The abstract reports models for both ages but never compares their predictive accuracy.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Single-cell transcriptomes were generated from the subventricular zone neurogenic region of 28 mice spanning young to old ages.
statements.evidence: single-cell transcriptomes from the subventricular zone neurogenic region of 28 mice, tiling ages from young to old
statements.note: The dataset covered 28 mice across the full young-to-old range.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The aging clocks generalized to independent mouse cohorts, other brain regions, and other species.
statements.evidence: These aging clocks are generalizable to independent cohorts of mice, other regions of the brains, and other species
statements.note: The clocks worked beyond the training data, across regions and species.
